purpose: V2-P01R §4 — decides MG0_TAG_POLICY and MG0_GLOSSARY_POLICY by tracing repository evidence, not by measuring accuracy.

code_evidence: src/t2s/grounding/schema_retriever.py:85-87 — SchemaRetriever._match_document_fields includes 'tags' and 'glossary_terms' as separately checked fields.
src/t2s/grounding/schema_retriever.py:105-113 — SchemaRetriever._score_document weights matched_field 'tags' at 1.5 and 'glossary_terms' at 1.75; this weight is applied to every retrieval.
src/t2s/grounding/schema_retriever.py:150-159 — InMemorySchemaSearch also joins tags and glossary_terms into the tokenized document text (raw match count feature).
src/t2s/grounding/grounding_context_builder.py:377-388 — _score_column includes catalog_column.tags and catalog_column.glossary_terms in the column token pool for token-overlap scoring.
src/t2s/catalog/metadata_document.py:44-45,53-54 — CatalogSearchDocumentBuilder projects both table.tags/glossary_terms and column.tags/glossary_terms into the search index.

src/t2s/solver/prompt_builder.py:104-136 — _format_authorized_schema (S0 baseline) DOES NOT emit tags or glossary_terms into the solver prompt. It emits only column identity + type + nullable/PK + description, plus relationship endpoints.
rationale.interpretation: Tags and glossary_terms are consumed by MG0's SchemaRetriever/RetrievalRanker/GroundingContextBuilder as deterministic retrieval-scoring features. They are NOT injected verbatim into the S0 solver prompt. Because MG0 is defined (Doc 04 §2) as SchemaRetriever + RelationshipExpander + GroundingBudget + S0 Serializer, the retrieval-scoring layer IS part of the MG0 information boundary. Excluding tags/glossary would change MG0 behaviour on legitimate metadata.

operational_consequences.for_provider_parity: Both providers must supply equivalent tags/glossary for logically equivalent metadata; otherwise retrieval scores drift and MG0 output diverges. The V2-P01R end-to-end parity test enforces this by construction (identical synthetic tags/glossary in Static and OpenMetadata fixtures).
operational_consequences.for_openmetadata_provider: OpenMetadataProvider must continue to map OM tags[source=Tag] to CatalogTable.tags/CatalogColumn.tags, and tags[source=Glossary] to CatalogTable.glossary_terms/CatalogColumn.glossary_terms. Suppressing them at the provider layer would silently downgrade MG0 retrieval quality on the OpenMetadata path.
operational_consequences.for_solver_prompt: No change — the S0 baseline serializer already omits tags and glossary_terms. V2-P01 §7's prohibition on 'glossary-derived business semantics' as solver evidence is upheld: they influence ranking, not prompt text.
operational_consequences.for_certification_lifecycle: Any future proposal to promote tags/glossary from retrieval-scoring feature to solver-prompt evidence must go through the Doc 04 §5 lifecycle (OFF → EXPERIMENTAL → SHADOW → CERTIFIED). V2-P01R does not perform that promotion.

alternative_option_rejected.option_B_rejected: Excluding tags/glossary from MG0 (as if they were not part of the baseline) would require code changes to SchemaRetriever._score_document and GroundingContextBuilder._score_column. That would be a semantic change to MG0 dressed as a governance decision — the phase charter forbids it (V2-P01R §6 'Do not force parity artificially. Do NOT: change ranking weights.').
alternative_option_rejected.why_A_is_the_correct_read: The MG0 baseline as it exists in this commit already reads tags/glossary. The invariant 'MG0 unchanged' means: do not change SchemaRetriever's ranking. Therefore tags/glossary must remain a retrieval-scoring feature, and the OpenMetadata path must feed them equivalently.

evidence: No benchmark-derived tags/glossary appear in tests/unit/catalog/test_mg0_provider_parity_end_to_end.py — the fixtures use synthetic identifiers only ('identity', 'core', 'customer', 'order').
Guard 2 (benchmark naming) and Guard 6 (prompt hygiene) in tests/unit/architecture/test_architecture_hygiene_guards.py forbid benchmark identifiers in production paths.
OpenMetadata is never written to by T2S, so benchmark-derived tags cannot be uploaded to OM by the runtime.
